comparator.name: Pedagogical Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: The annual catalogue gives 60 EC in year one, 60 EC in the common second year, and 20 EC of Upbringing and Development, 25 EC of electives and a 15 EC bachelor project in year three. The 2026–2027 transition notes replace the previous introductory research and SPSS courses with Research Methods 1A and 1B, which teach descriptive and inferential statistics using SPSS. Year-two course descriptions still name the earlier content as expected knowledge. The bachelor project requires all first-year courses, the second research practicum and the second-year study-design course. Limited exceptions require approval. Students conduct applied empirical research in teams and submit advice and individual assessed work.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic target names Pedagogical Sciences rather than a third-year specialisation. Leiden offers Education Sciences, Upbringing and Development, and Orthopedagogy of Upbringing and Education. Upbringing and Development retains the programme’s broad child-development and family/upbringing identity across ordinary and vulnerable development without narrowing the route to classroom education or clinical orthopedagogy. This selection was fixed before any UCR course was considered.

alternativeSelection.assessment: This option integrates lifespan development, cognition, social context, psychological assessment, youth resilience and research. A separate child and family or clinical option would reuse the same substantive core without a sustained different course sequence. A school-focused option lacks sustained instruction, classroom design and teacher practice. Digital media adds context without a dedicated child-development and digital education sequence.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce developmental psychology. UCR combines development with broader study of the brain and behaviour.
Both study cognition and learning. UCR uses cognitive neuroscience to examine higher mental functions.
Both use biology to explain behaviour. Leiden applies this to child development, while UCR studies nervous systems more broadly.
Both address developmental differences. UCR follows physical, cognitive and social change across the lifespan.
Leiden introduces child rearing as a field of pedagogical study.
Leiden applies introductory psychology to educational questions.
Both examine social contexts and inequality. Leiden focuses on intercultural upbringing and education.
Leiden introduces theories and methods specific to education sciences.
Both study psychological difficulties. UCR covers mental health across the lifespan, while Leiden introduces clinical child and educational contexts.
UCR students design and refine rhetoric activities for primary-school pupils. Leiden applies pedagogical research to practice more broadly.
Both cover tests and assessment, including how to judge measurement quality. Leiden applies these methods to upbringing and education.
Both examine young people’s development beyond the family. UCR focuses on radicalisation, protective factors and educational prevention.
Leiden has a dedicated course on development within the family.
Leiden trains students in approaches to guiding caregivers and preventing problems.
Leiden studies learning and behavioural difficulties in educational settings.
Both teach research design and statistics. UCR applies these methods in a student research project.
Both develop statistical and research skills. UCR focuses on experimental design and analysis in health and behaviour.
Both develop skills for evaluating research evidence. UCR focuses on systematic reviews and meta-analysis, while Leiden also trains students to design a study.
Both teach qualitative research. UCR covers study design, interviewing and analysis.
Leiden requires a further research practicum in pedagogical sciences.
Leiden requires a 15 EC applied bachelor project with team research and individual assessed work. UCR’s optional independent research sits outside the 180 EC schedule.
Both develop academic and professional skills. Leiden provides tutoring within Pedagogical Sciences.
Both develop communication skills. UCR studies rhetoric and persuasion, while Leiden practises professional conversations.
Both develop ethical reasoning. Leiden also applies legal and ethical principles to child rearing and development.
Both develop communication skills. UCR studies persuasion and public communication, while Leiden practises conversations in pedagogical settings.
Leiden has a dedicated course in critical reasoning and academic writing for pedagogical sciences.
Leiden applies philosophical reasoning to questions about education and upbringing.
Leiden includes programme-specific orientation to professional practice.
Leiden focuses on family factors in clinical child and adolescent studies.
Leiden practises systematic observation of child behaviour and interaction.
Leiden reserves 25 EC for open elective study.

notes.text: Leiden studies upbringing and education directly through caregiver guidance, observation, communication labs and a project with a pedagogical organisation. UCR approaches related questions through psychology, cognition, sociology and research. Its primary-school communication project gives practice designing rhetoric activities for pupils.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden studies how children develop at home, at school and in other settings. The Upbringing and Development specialisation examines behaviour, caregiver guidance and development inside and outside the family. Students finish with an applied research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR option brings together developmental psychology, cognition and language, psychological assessment and youth resilience. It includes a primary-school communication project. Leiden provides a dedicated sequence in child rearing, caregiver guidance, professional conversations and applied pedagogical research.
